brief: Piper Sandler estimates September payrolls rose +60k, below the +90k consensus and down from August's strong +162k print, because the August boost from state and local education hiring (a summer-recess seasonal-adjustment effect) is likely to evaporate in September. Despite the weaker headline, underlying signals point to healthy, broadening job growth: ADP's September private employment measure rose +90k (vs. +75k consensus, August revised down to +36k), its weekly tracker has shifted higher, initial claims are extremely low, continuing claims are rangebound, and the employment diffusion index has ticked up. A composite of regional Fed manufacturing future-employment plans near its cycle high signals stronger manufacturing hiring ahead, and data-center construction is lifting nonresidential construction employment, while residential construction stays weak on depressed homebuilder confidence and worsening affordability. The firm sees the unemployment rate holding at 4.1%, matching consensus, even as the Conference Board's Jobs Hard-Jobs Easy metric keeps climbing. The covered unemployment rate sits at a historically low 1.1%. Average hourly earnings are seen at +0.3% m/m (matching consensus and August) and accelerating to 3.2% y/y versus 3.1% consensus, with wage growth likely to steady going forward, tracking JOLTS quit-rate stabilization, with potential 2027 reacceleration.
